hero.title: Weddings in Sri Lanka
hero.body: Grand celebrations, quiet beach ceremonies and mornings for just the two of you. We look after the guests, the venues and the days, so you can be at your own wedding.
hero.alt: A couple walking a palm-lined beach at sunset

why.heading: A short flight. A setting nobody has seen before.
paragraphs: Sri Lanka is a short direct flight from India's major cities and an easy stop between Europe and Australia. Your guests arrive on a single flight, and the island feels a world away when they land.
Beaches without crowds, colonial mansions, temples lit at night and tea estates in the clouds, all within a few hours of each other, and hosts who have looked after visitors for generations.

styles.heading: Four ways to marry here.
styles.body: Each one is a starting point. Tell us yours and we will shape it.

settings.heading: Where it could happen.
settings.body: The settings our couples choose most, each a short drive from the next.

items.name: Bentota and the west coast
items.line: Wide beaches and river lawns an hour from the airport. Our most-asked setting for pheras on the sand.
items.alt: A lone walker on a wide, empty beach

items.name: Galle Fort and the south
items.line: Ramparts above the sea, colonial villas and lantern-lit streets for the evening after.
items.alt: A lit café street inside Galle Fort at night

items.name: Tangalle and the deep south
items.line: Long, quiet beaches and private villas for smaller weddings that want the coast to themselves.
items.alt: A lone walker on an empty stretch of the south coast

items.name: Kandy
items.line: The hill capital, its lake and the Temple of the Tooth. Grand hotels and Kandyan drummers.
items.alt: The Temple of the Tooth across the lake in Kandy at dusk

items.name: Tea country
items.line: Estate bungalows above the clouds, cool evenings and a fire after dinner. For elopements and small parties.
items.alt: Rows of tea around an estate bungalow on a hillside

questions.q: Can foreign couples marry legally in Sri Lanka?
questions.a: Yes. A local registrar can register your marriage. You will need passports, birth certificates, proof that you are free to marry and a police clearance, certified and legalised at home. We send the current list for your nationality and handle the local side.

questions.q: Do you replace our wedding planner?
questions.a: No. Many couples bring their own planner, and we work alongside them as the team on the ground. If you do not have one, we introduce suppliers we trust.

questions.q: How many guests can you look after?
questions.a: From two to several hundred. The larger the wedding, the earlier we need to start, because venues for big parties book up first.

questions.q: When is the best time of year?
questions.a: November to April is dry on the west and south coasts. From May to September, the hill country and the east coast are the better settings.
Every wedding is quoted after the brief, with guest travel, venues and suppliers listed separately so you can see where the money goes.
